_note: The 'Has all functionality' rows (C10, C18) run each group's drivers from the drivers/ folder next to this file (copies of CS212-CourseMaterials' Lab01-Python/Group<X>/drivers, which are the master copies; refresh them with: node bin/sync-drivers.js <that Lab01-Python folder> configs/CS212/Lab01, add --check to only compare). Set LAB_STRICT=1 in the grading environment once the instructions fix the function names (see the _draft instructions). The base testCheck entries are placeholders for a group with no drivers (NEEDS MANUAL CHECK). llm_check rows use DeepSeek through the OpenAI-compatible API (llmCheck): the API key comes from LLM_API_KEY or this machine's configs/local-config.json (main menu: Settings → AI grading checks; grading asks for it and stops without it). This sends student code, including names in header comments, to DeepSeek. The 'No run-time errors' rows (C12, C20) are build_check: for Python that is a syntax check only; crashes show up as failures in the functionality rows. developer_comments rows require a name and a date in EACH file (scope each); 'Brian Bird' header lines (starter files) are ignored. llmCheck.model is pinned so the config does not depend on a machine's local-config. Lint rows (C14, C22) lint only their part's files: each group's variations.<X>.overrides.lint.parts gives a filePattern per part (the same word the group's drivers use to find that program, matched against file text or path, case-insensitive); the base lint.parts are placeholders for a student whose group is unknown (those rows say NEEDS MANUAL CHECK). A file matching a part's pattern is linted for that part; comments list errors then warnings by file and line, without rule codes. The llm_check rows (C11, C13 / C19, C21) carry partId too, so each reads only its part's files (the same lint.parts).
